item.text: {"text":"Closest direct match: [HSTU-BLaIR (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10545) enriches HSTU item representations with textual metadata embeddings and reports improvements on two Amazon Reviews 2023 domains. However, it uses a pretrained BLaIR encoder; its results do not establish that text encoders learned from scratch improve sparse-item ranking. [SimRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.22136v1) provides complementary evidence: title-derived similarity distributions supervise next-item scores through an auxiliary loss, helping rare items without adding inference parameters. Its experiments also use pretrained text embeddings and a SASRec backbone, so transferring the loss to HSTU remains a hypothesis.\n\nA constraint-compatible experiment would retain HSTU and represent each item with an ID embedding plus projected title/description features from a small, randomly initialized token encoder, jointly optimized by next-item training. Shared token embeddings and mean pooling offer a low-cost starting point; ID dropout could encourage content use. These are proposed adaptations, not verified findings from the cited papers. [DenseRec (2025)](https://earl-workshop.github.io/pdf/recsys2025-workshops_paper_167.pdf) supports preserving collaborative identity alongside content, while warning that semantic similarity alone can miss contextual relevance; it likewise relies on pretrained content embeddings. Treat explicit model numbers and compatibility phrases in available text as learnable evidence, never as guaranteed compatibility labels. Validate against ID-only HSTU using the fixed macro HR@10, with training-frequency breakdowns for diagnosis. The located evidence supports testing this single-network design, but does not demonstrate gains under the exact no-pretraining constraint."}
